A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same three-experiment study. Their complete main texts, tables, figures and Appendices A–B are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v3 reports original GPT-4o prompting experiments, comparisons across four model families and repeated Public Goods Game simulations, including appendix results.

after.justification: v4 retains these original experiments and simulations and adds Qwen3-30B results across all six economic games.

M1.justification: The step-count-controlled chain-of-thought procedure, retries and reflection using prior responses are retained. The five-step example is clarified as model-generated output. Qwen is an additional evaluated model, without a new proposed algorithm or architecture.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same six English-language economic games, repeated Public Goods interactions and resource-endowment scenarios. Adding Qwen changes the evaluated models, without adding data domains, tasks or environmental conditions.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds Qwen3-30B without and with extended thinking as a fifth matched comparison pair. All four earlier model-family pairs remain in the corresponding six-game comparisons.

E3.justification: Game payoffs, response options, trial counts, group compositions and ten-round simulations are retained. Qwen follows the existing evaluation design. The full-history description and explanation of normalization by the 100-point endowment clarify settings rather than establish protocol changes.

E4.justification: The reasoning-length, reflection, group-composition and endowment analyses are retained. v3 Figure 10 becomes v4 Figure 11 unchanged. The new Qwen figure reports standard model comparisons; warm-starting and answer-order randomization are proposed future work, without new tests.

E5.justification: Section 4.2 newly describes the retained 100 trials per model-game pair as independent. This is a limited reporting clarification, without a stated increase in runs or changes to the existing SD/SEM and significance-test reporting practices.

E6.justification: Table 1 and new Figure 10 add Qwen results across six games. Without/with thinking, mean Dictator allocation is 0.500/0.099, Public Goods cooperation is 64/100 versus 0/100, and third-party punishment is 100/100 versus 59/100. All earlier model scores, plotted results and repeated-game findings are retained.

T1.justification: The game and payoff definitions are unchanged, and neither version presents formal theorems or proofs. The added normalization explanation restates an existing empirical metric rather than introducing mathematical reasoning.

C1.justification: The conclusion drops v3's blanket statement of reduced norm-enforcing behavior and focuses on lower cooperation and collective performance. This narrowing is partial: the abstract still claims reduced norm enforcement. The central cooperation and group-payoff contributions remain.

C2.justification: Section 2.2 shifts cross-model interpretation from causal impact to association, and Section 2.1 distinguishes deliberation length from reasoning quality. Section 7 adds answer-position bias and a second-order-dilemma explanation for variable punishment, alongside suggestions for cooperative warm-starting.

D1.justification: v4 newly states that all experimental data are open-sourced and supplies a Hugging Face access link. It also specifies access to full interaction histories and Qwen access through Alibaba Cloud. Existing prompts, hardware, token budgets and runtime disclosures remain; external data availability was not verified.

R1.justification: Section 5 adds prior LLM economic-game studies by Jia, Gandhi, Guo and Akata and reframes competitive-bias discussion around training and evaluation benchmarks. Model documentation, warm-starting and answer-bias references also expand the context, while the central research positioning remains.

P1.justification: Substantial paragraph-level rewriting spans Sections 2–7, especially related work, interpretation of repeated-game results and limitations. The reasoning example becomes a displayed numbered list, and explanations and terminology are revised throughout. Section order remains, but the prose revision extends well beyond isolated copyediting.

P2.justification: Table 1 gains Qwen rows, Appendix B gains Figure 10, and captions are clarified. Existing figures are relocated and the appendix layout is rearranged, with the endowment plot renumbered Figure 11. All earlier figure graphics are unchanged, and the two-column presentation remains.

improvement.justification: The Qwen replication modestly strengthens the evidence, while more cautious cross-model attribution, specific limitations and new data-access information improve interpretation and reproducibility documentation. The gains are limited: the abstract still generalizes reduced punishment despite the DeepSeek and Claude exceptions acknowledged in Section 4.2 and Table 1.
